shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The love-strong-as-death declaration opens on the ascent question rather than on the seal imperative: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.8.5, skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5) 'who is this coming up from the wilderness', turning within the same verse to second-masculine-singular address, עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ and יְלָדַֽתְךָ (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier) 'I awakened you' / 'she who bore you' — an intra-verse turn from the third-feminine-singular question to first-person/second-masculine-singular address that is disclosed here rather than resolved. That same 1cs/2ms address chain continues unbroken into the next verse: her imperative שִׂימֵ֨נִי (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) 'set me', addressed to לִבֶּ֗ךָ and זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) 'your heart' and 'your arm', carries the same 2ms suffix as עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ and יְלָדַֽתְךָ — no gendered form changes across the MT 8:5|8:6 join, and no vocative or imperative onset marks a new addressee there, so nothing licenses a cut at it. The span instead opens on the attested oath anchor at its own front seam: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Song.8.4, byte tier) 'I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem', turning the address to the daughters, against which MT 8:5 opens a fresh third-feminine-singular voice on the ascent formula — a genuine speaker turn. WEB: “I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem...” (web:Song.8.4); “Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you.” (web:Song.8.5). The gnomic peak follows without a marked seam, כִּֽי עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) 'for love is strong as death', closing on the divided token pair שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְ יָֽה (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier; OSHB divides one WLC word into shalhevet + yah for exegesis, tagging the second element as lemma 3050) — the intensive-suffix-versus-divine-element crux, held rather than decided. WEB: “...a very flame of Yah.” (web:Song.8.6). Verse oshb:Song.8.7 continues the same gnomic claim without a voice-shift marker; the mark layer places no seg between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7, so the span closes on the MT 8:7 seg (single-witness, disclosed as corroboration only), immediately before אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) opens a first-person-plural speaker group at the span's own back edge.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ratifying the cut between MT 8:5 and MT 8:6 on the mood or speech-act change from question to address was the leading rejected alternative: no gendered form changes across that seam and no vocative or imperative onset marks a new addressee there, so the absence of any tier-1 marker at it stands unrebutted. The intra-verse turn inside MT 8:5 itself, from third-feminine-singular question to 1cs/2ms address, is a disclosure duty rather than a boundary, since it occurs within a single verse.

shipped_row.device_notes: The shalhevet-yah pair (MT 8:6) is a classic crux (OSHB exegesis note, single-witness apparatus): the construal (intensive 'mighty flame' versus divine element) is held, not decided, and the one-word/divided-token fact is disclosed on this citation; this is the Yah-form surface (sweep: 1 verse) in a book carrying zero plain YHWH/Elohim citations (sweep: 0 of 117 verses, byte-swept). The mi-zot formula at MT 8:5 is the ascent-run member (skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5), a distinct object from the bare mi-zot interrogative (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) — the two counts are never blended. The span opens on this ascent formula and a 1cs/2ms address chain before it reaches the aphoristic peak at MT 8:6, a deviation from the exemplar epigram shape retained under the same category because no tier-1 marker separates the opening question and address from the peak that follows.

prev_row.device_notes: Formula-variation discipline: the mah-ta'iru variant lacks the gazelle-and-doe pairing carried by the fuller form at web:Song.2.7 and web:Song.3.5, and its verb is written defective, תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ (oshb:Song.8.4, byte tier), where the fuller form is written plene, תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ (oshb:Song.2.7, byte tier) and תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ (oshb:Song.3.5, byte tier) — the two plene tokens are byte-identical to one another. This variant is distinguished from the shape held at web:Song.5.8 = oshb:Song.5.8 (the third of exactly four adjuration sites in the book), which carries a conditional clause, אִֽם תִּמְצְאוּ֙ 'if you find', and a separate interrogative clause, מַה תַּגִּ֣ידוּ 'what will you tell', both without the gazelle-and-doe pairing either; this row's own verse, oshb:Song.8.4, is the fourth and last, never blended with the daughters' quoted-back oath at web:Song.5.9.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The brothers' deliberation opens with a 1cp possessive, אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) 'a little sister [belongs] to us', marking a new speaker-group distinct from the woman's own 1cs voice throughout the surrounding movements (this achot token is role-split from the bride-epithet achoti used earlier in the book) — the sister here is theirs, not his address to her; the speaker-group identification itself is a content inference rather than a named form, though the keeper-and-vineyard chain at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same 'my mother's sons' phrase, links the same group across the book.
